problem: Find the degree of the homogeneous function $f(x,y)=\frac{{x}^{2}}{{y}^{3}-{x}^{3}}\,\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{x}{y}).$
worked_solution:
A function $f(x,y)$ is homogeneous of degree $n$ if it satisfies the property

$$
f(tx,ty)={t}^{n}f(x,y).
$$

So first, we compute $h(tx,ty),$ and then we simplify by writing it as ${t}^{n}f(x,y)$ for some $n$:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(tx,ty) & =\frac{(tx)^{2}}{(ty)^{3}-(tx)^{3}}\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{tx}{ty}) \\  & =\frac{{t}^{2}{x}^{2}}{{t}^{3}{y}^{3}-{t}^{3}{x}^{3}}\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{tx}{ty}) \\  & =\frac{{t}^{2}{x}^{2}}{{t}^{3}({y}^{3}-{x}^{3})}\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{tx}{ty}) \\  & =\frac{{t}^{2}}{{t}^{3}}\cdot \frac{{x}^{2}}{{y}^{3}-{x}^{3}}\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{x}{y}) \\  & =\frac{1}{t}\cdot \frac{{x}^{2}}{{y}^{3}-{x}^{3}}\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{x}{y}) \\  & =\frac{1}{t}f(x,y)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
f(tx,ty)=\frac{1}{t}\cdot f(x,y)={t}^{-1}f(x,y)
$$

and so the degree of the homogeneous function $f(x,y)$ is $-1.$
